# Poker Dance

> Play Texas hold 'em in real life, but without a deck. Phones are the cards, a shared screen is the table.

Poker Dance is for people sitting around the same table. It replaces the deck,
not the game: one screen shows the community cards, everyone else holds their
hole cards on their own phone. Chips, betting and conversation stay physical.

Everyone opens the same URL — the site plus any table name, like
`https://poker.dance/kitchen`. The first device to open it becomes the table
screen; every device after that gets a seat. Adding `?table` forces a device to
be the table screen, and the flag drops out of the address bar so the URL stays
the one you hand around for seats.

Gestures, since nothing on screen spells them out:

- Table screen: move the dealer button to deal a new hand; tap the board to
  cycle through flop, turn, river, and hidden again.
- A seat: pull down to peek at your hole cards, all the way down to reveal
  them, swipe up to fold, and tap to take a fold back.

## Pages

- [Poker Dance](https://poker.dance/): what it is, and a button that opens a new table.
- [Hand rankings](https://poker.dance/learn/hand-rankings): the ten hands, each dealt from the real deck rather than drawn as pictures, with how often you hold one after the flop, the turn and the river. A chooser turns "your hand" into "anyone at the table", from one player up to ten. One player is exactly enumerated; more than one is simulated, because hands at a table share a board and are not independent.

## Deliberately not included

- No chips, pots, or betting. Those work better as real chips on a real table.
- No remote play. The app assumes everyone is in the same room.
- No accounts, names, or history. A table is one night in one room.
